keyChanges.title: Taylor AI6 trial still ahead of Samsung, and only maybe in December
keyChanges.description: The Korea Herald reported on Nov. 8 that Samsung is still installing tools and running performance checks at its Taylor, Texas foundry, and that trial operations could start only in mid-to-late December. Samsung has not confirmed that date. Spokesperson Michele Glaze said in late October that the first Taylor plant is expected to be fully operational by year-end, with the production ramp in 2027. The Herald says Taylor is where Tesla's AI6 would be made under the existing $16.5 billion supply deal, and that those chips are planned for the second half of 2027. Construction started in 2022 against an original second-half 2024 operations target, so the project is about two years late. That undercuts mid-September industry reports that Taylor had already started 2nm AI5 trial wafers and would finish mass-production verification by year-end for supply next year. No yield, shipment, or new tape-out was disclosed. A second Taylor fab is still only 'expected' to break ground this month; the AMD and Nvidia base-die talk attached to it is not a Tesla order and was already reported.

positive_signals: Tool install and line checks are underway, and Samsung has said the first Taylor plant should be fully operational by the end of 2026
AI6 is still tied to the $16.5 billion Taylor agreement, with a stated second-half 2027 production window
negative_signals: The December trial date is unnamed industry sourcing; Samsung has not confirmed it or said wafers are running
Conflicts with mid-September reports that AI5 trial wafers were already in production and that supply could start next year
Original Taylor operations target was the second half of 2024; the Herald puts the slip at about two years
No yield, sample shipment, or new tape-out this week
Commercial AI6 output is still not until the second half of 2027, so 2nm volume is not a 2026 event
TrendForce Q2 foundry share cited in the same report is still 5.9% for Samsung versus 72.5% for TSMC

keyChanges.title: Giga Texas 4680 'largest plant' claim is a hiring post, not new GWh
keyChanges.description: On November 9, 2026, Tesla director of cell manufacturing operations Michael Guilfoy posted on X that the Austin 4680 team is growing as it increases the ramp and now supports four vehicle programs: Model Y, Cybertruck, Cybercab, and Semi. He said a 'massive expansion' will 'soon' make Giga Texas the largest battery-cell plant in North America, and he listed senior production, quality, engineering, maintenance, and supervisor openings. TeslaNorth (November 10), Basenor (updated November 9), and Drive Tesla Canada all restated that post. None of them, and not Guilfoy, gave a completion date or a new capacity figure. The Q3 2026 update still lists Texas 4680 installed capacity at more than 40 GWh — the same installed, not measured-output, line carried from Q2 — and says cells are being increased for Cybercab, Semi, and higher Model Y volume while battery availability still limits how fast vehicle output can rise. 'Largest in North America' is a forecast inside a recruiting post, not a ranked production result.

positive_signals: The cell-manufacturing director says the Austin ramp is increasing and the team is hiring across leadership, engineering, and technicians
Model Y, Cybertruck, Cybercab, and Semi are explicitly assigned to the in-house 4680 line
negative_signals: No new GWh and no completion date; 'largest in North America' is an unverified forecast
Official installed capacity is unchanged at more than 40 GWh and is still not measured output
Q3 still says battery availability limits vehicle production, so four programs are drawing on a line Tesla has not shown can clear that constraint
Calling Cybertruck a 'growing' program is a demand claim with no volume attached

keyChanges.title: Berlin 4680 cells still finished in Texas; full local start aimed at mid-2027
keyChanges.description: At the November 11, 2026 Automobilwoche Kongress, Giga Berlin plant director André Thierig said Tesla's own cell production in Grünheide is supposed to start fully in mid-2027. The cell hall is already standing, and the plant is already making anode and cathode electrodes, but those electrodes are still shipped to Texas, made into cells there, and sent back to Germany. Ending that round trip is the mid-2027 goal, not a line that is running now. That sharpens the October 2 Battery-News account, already on file, which said 4680 output in Grünheide would start in 2027 and ramp toward 18 GWh — the planned capacity tied to the May 2026 $250 million and 1,500-job announcement. The 18 GWh figure is still a plan, not output. Thierig also described German cell production as a site decision despite better economics in China and North America. Q3 still classifies Berlin 4680 as in construction. His same-day comments on 7,500 Model Ys a week and an undecided second vehicle hall are vehicle-plant items, not a cell result.

Mid-2027 is a dated target from the plant director for ending the Texas cell round trip, reported by Automobilwoche and TeslaNorth

keyChanges.title: Invite-only Cybercab orders open at $29,990, but the car will not run without a $299 subscription
keyChanges.description: Late on Nov. 13 Tesla invited select customers to order a Cybercab for personal use at an estimated $29,990 before tax, with a $1,000 non-refundable deposit and an estimated December 2026 delivery. It is not a public order page. The order screen requires an Autonomy Subscription, shown at $299 a month with the first month included, and the contract says the car will not operate without an active subscription. Reported terms limit use to personal, non-commercial trips: Robotaxi-network, ride-hail, delivery, and rental use need separate written Tesla authorization, so a personal sale does not add a paid robotaxi. Operation is confined to Tesla robotaxi geofences the company can shrink, resale without permission carries contractual damages of at least $50,000 plus a Tesla repurchase right, and the only manual move is about 2 mph. Ashok Elluswamy said a personal Cybercab would run unsupervised inside the same geofences as Robotaxi, serving the owner. Invitees were shown delivery choices that include Austin, Dallas, Houston, San Antonio, and Fort Worth; that is a delivery list, not evidence that paid Cybercab service has left Austin. Musk then called $299 too high and said it should be closer to about $115 a month, and that nationwide use still waits on regulatory approval. Texas Cybercab authorizations are unchanged at 573.

keyChanges.title: San Antonio Robotaxi announced Nov. 9 with no fleet size and no Cybercab
keyChanges.description: On Nov. 9 Tesla's Robotaxi account said service would be available in San Antonio at 5 a.m., with a launch-geofence map. TeslaNorth treats it as the fifth Texas city after Austin, Dallas, Fort Worth, and Houston. Tesla did not say how many vehicles, whether any would be Cybercabs, or whether a safety monitor would be aboard. TechCrunch noted those same gaps and said prior non-Austin fleets have been a handful to a few dozen vehicles. Electrek, citing Robotaxi Tracker, put the advertised polygon near 274 square miles, said San Antonio International is inside the drawing but not served, and reported zero Tesla robotaxis logged in the city on Monday morning. By Nov. 14 the tracker's 30-day community floor was 11 Model Y vehicles and zero Cybercabs. Paid Cybercab service is still not evidenced outside Austin. Square miles are not a fleet.

keyChanges.title: Robotaxi hours go 24/7 in current cities, without new cars or new markets
keyChanges.description: Tesla's Robotaxi account said the service now runs 24/7 in every city where it is already available, ahead of the year-end target Ashok Elluswamy gave on the October earnings call. TeslaNorth dates the post to the night of Nov. 11; the embedded post is time-stamped Nov. 12. The change closes the overnight shutdown. Days earlier, rider screenshots showed a 5 a.m. to 2 a.m. window, including Dallas, and Tesla's support page says hours can vary by area, so that step was not proof of a network-wide schedule. The 24/7 post did not add a city, open highways, or disclose vehicles. A trip still has to fall inside the geofence and a car still has to be free.

keyChanges.title: Austin Robotaxi polygon grows again; square miles are a tracker estimate
keyChanges.description: On Nov. 9 Tesla's Robotaxi account said a bigger Austin service area was live. A wider boundary does not say how many cars are available, and it follows the prior week's camera hits outside the old geofence, which were not themselves paid trips.

keyChanges.title: Finland Clears Supervised Assisted Driving; EU-Wide Approval Is Next Year
keyChanges.description: On 11 November Traficom said Tesla may immediately start offering Tesla Assisted Driving in Finland, and Tesla Europe posted that rollout begins soon. TeslaNorth and Tesla Oracle count this as the 11th EU recognition of the Dutch RDW file, after the Netherlands and the nine states RDW had already notified (Belgium, Denmark, Estonia, Croatia, Latvia, Lithuania, Slovenia, Slovakia, Czechia). It is not unsupervised. AFP, quoting Traficom, said the car can be driven without hands on the controls, but the driver keeps sole legal responsibility and must watch the road and be ready to take over. Specialist Jukka Juhola said the assisted-driving name describes the system's true nature, and that cars where responsibility leaves the driver are a later step. Traficom put final EU-wide approval next year, not this quarter, and said the early Finnish permission is a chance to learn the system before the hardest winter. Drive Tesla also quoted Juhola that snow, slush or dirt on the cameras can limit operation. No customer-car activation date was given. Germany, France, Italy and the UK are still outside the patchwork.

Tesla Europe said the feature is now approved in Finland and that rollout begins soon
It is a new national recognition beyond the ten countries already on the Dutch file
negative_signals: Still supervised driver assistance: the driver is legally responsible and must constantly watch the road
Traficom said final EU-wide approval is expected next year, after the October target already slipped

Tesla gave no date that Finnish customer cars are actually running it; large markets remain out

key_metrics.actual: 11th EU recognition of Dutch supervised TAD; not a confirmed live Finnish fleet
key_metrics.trajectory: Traficom puts the bloc decision next year

keyChanges.title: Korea Says Tesla's China-Built FSD Exemption File Is Still Incomplete
keyChanges.description: Drive Tesla, citing Korea JoongAng Daily and a 4 November CBS Nocut comment, reported this week that the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport still cannot review Tesla Korea's exemption for Full Self-Driving on China-built cars because a substantial part of the technical file is missing. Officials said there is no international FSD standard and that the review will take considerable time even after the documents arrive. The same coverage says owners have been flooding Land Minister Hong Ji-sun's posts demanding the restriction be lifted. Of 238,968 Teslas registered in Korea at the end of September, only 53,477 (22.4%) were eligible; 183,407 China-built cars cannot use the feature. U.S.-built cars qualify under the Korea-U.S. FTA, while China-built cars must meet domestic rules that include hands on the wheel. A National Assembly petition with 23,315 signatures asks for approval by hardware, software and safety rather than factory. This is a separate stall from last week's KFTC marketing complaint, and it is not an approval.

key_metrics.target: Exemption so China-built cars can use FSD

keyChanges.title: Tesla Threatens a Chinese Outlet Over Grey-Market FSD That Is Still Unapproved
keyChanges.description: CarNewsChina, citing Jiemian, reported on 11 November that Tesla sent D1EV a legal notice over a Changsha driving competition that used a Model Y with an unofficially activated copy of supervised FSD. Tesla called the activation illegal hacking that bypasses regional restrictions and enables features not approved for China, and it demanded the tests stop, the videos come down, VINs within 48 hours, and the cars restored to factory settings, warning of criminal charges. D1EV's CEO refused and said the point was to push regulators to approve the supervised system. The article says many owners have paid 64,000 yuan and still cannot use the North American feature set, while grey-market unlocks sell for about 140 dollars. Tesla China had no further public comment. This is a legal fight over an unapproved system, not a certification.

positive_signals: Tesla is treating unapproved China activation as a violation rather than quietly tolerating it
negative_signals: Supervised FSD is still not approved for commercial use in China

keyChanges.title: Europe 2026.39.100 is still v14.2.2.7 and quietly caps speed offset
keyChanges.description: Software package 2026.39.100, released November 11 and reported November 12, is Europe's customer build and it is FSD (Supervised) v14.2.2.7, not v14.3 and not v15. Tesla's release notes only rename FSD (Supervised) to Tesla Assisted Driving and say the change 'does not change the way your features behave.' Not a Tesla App's notes page and a November 12 owner report say that is false: maximum Speed Offset dropped from +50% to +10% and resets to 0% at the start of every drive, so the over-limit setting does not persist. Basenor independently described the same 2026.39.100 / v14.2.2.7 package and the same user-reported cap. The cut implements limits regulators already demanded; it is not a new driving model. TeslaFi's global sample showed only 233 cars (1.9%) on this build, which is a tracker slice of a regional rollout, not proof the EU fleet has it. North American customers on 2026.38.5.x are already on v14.3.13. A Finland snow clip of v14.2.2.7 is a supervised demo, not a capability or approval milestone. v15 is still not in a customer OTA.

keyChanges.title: Tesla SI vehicle-operator reqs are still hourly FSD safety drivers
keyChanges.description: LinkedIn shows seven new Tesla requisitions titled SI Vehicle Operator, Self-Driving posted 8–13 Nov 2026: Tampa (8 Nov), San Francisco and Charlotte (9 Nov), Reno (10 Nov), Los Angeles (12 Nov), and Santa Ana and Doral (13 Nov). The Santa Ana, Tampa, Charlotte, and San Francisco descriptions match. The seat is an SI Safety Operator on the Vehicle FSD (Supervised) team: drive a prototype 6–8 hours a day in FSD and in manual, collect audio and camera data, and write a daily drive report. Pay is an hourly base plus a 10–15% night differential, with full-time benefits. The posting does not say one-year or temporary. The same title was already up before this window in Decatur (30 Oct), San Antonio (4 Nov), and Orlando (5 Nov), so this is the template spreading to more cities, not a new program. A related Munro, Michigan SI Safety Operator posted 13 Nov adds ride-hailing oversight and requires English and Spanish, but it is still a driving and data-collection seat. None of these are autonomy engineers.

keyChanges.title: New robotaxi reqs are city managers and night-shift staff, not autonomy engineers

keyChanges.title: J.P. Morgan humanoid forecast names Tesla and still gives Optimus no volume
keyChanges.description: J.P. Morgan told clients on Nov. 12 that U.S. humanoid production could reach 300,000–400,000 units by 2030 and about 1.5 million by 2035, as the industry moves from demonstrations into manufacturing, logistics, and warehousing. Reuters reported the note. The bank said most U.S. manufacturers other than Tesla are targeting only 10,000–30,000 robots a year, and it listed Optimus with Digit, Atlas, Figure, and Apollo as key platforms. It published no Tesla build rate, no price, and no customer. It said near-term progress is still supply-constrained, with hands, actuators, the AI “brain,” and production capacity as binding bottlenecks, plus limits on training data and compute. A multi-shift robot might save a customer about $100,000 a year on the bank’s estimate, and parts such as actuators, motors, and vision could be a ~$30 billion market by 2035, with near-term value in suppliers rather than robot makers. The note itself was not published, and the Reuters account does not say whether 300,000–400,000 is an annual run-rate or a cumulative stock. Nothing in the note opens the Austin plant, sets a rental price, or shows robots leaving Fremont for outside customers.

positive_signals: J.P. Morgan treats Tesla as the U.S. humanoid maker outside the 10,000–30,000-a-year band it assigns to other domestic manufacturers

keyChanges.title: China October retail falls to 8,817, lowest since July 2022
keyChanges.description: CPCA figures published November 9 put Tesla's China retail sales at 8,817 in October, down 66.10% year over year and 86.40% from September's 64,837. That is the fifth straight year-over-year retail decline, the first month under 10,000 since July 2022 (8,461), and the lowest NEV share since April 2022 at 0.80% (5.98% in September, 2.03% a year earlier). BEV share was 1.15%. Shanghai exports of 59,012 rose 66.27% year over year and 93.30% from September and were a record 87% of the already-reported 67,829 wholesale total, so the export book masked a domestic crash. January-October retail is 389,905, down 15.00% year over year, worse than the 11.93% decline through September. Exports over the same period are 420,984, up 101.28%, and now exceed domestic retail; they are 51.92% of year-to-date wholesale of 810,889. Tesla dropped out of October's NEV retail top 10 (fourth in September) and the overall passenger top 10, and fell from fifth to seventh in the year-to-date NEV ranking, with share down to 4.4% from 4.9% through September. On exports it rose to a 10.1% NEV-export share (5.4% in September) and fifth in overall passenger exports. The October 30 financing offer, with down payments cut to 39,900 yuan through November 30, was already in the market and did not hold October retail. Q4 still has no Tesla delivery guide, and this CPCA split is a monthly China print, not an IR production or delivery total.

keyChanges.title: Cybertruck deposits face refunds as cheaper trims close and Cyberbeast rises to $109,990
keyChanges.description: On November 9 Elon Musk wrote that the Cybertruck order rate far exceeds the production rate and that Tesla will have to return deposits for a lot of people. The November 7 plan to add a shift before dismantling the Giga Texas line around June or July 2027 was already in place, and the refund post did not move that changeover. He disputed an unprofitable-truck framing and gave no truck profit figure, order count, or refund count. The same day Tesla's U.S. configurator greyed out Dual Motor AWD at $82,490 and Premium AWD at $92,490. Cyberbeast was the only selectable new order, and its price rose $7,500 from $102,490 to $109,990, about 7.3%. An earlier Monday Seattle check still showed a January-March 2027 Cyberbeast window at the old price. Musk also said building more factory space is hard and that prototypes are trivial by comparison. This is a genuine step past the November 6 mid-2027 wind-down: buyers are now being told many existing orders will be refunded, and the orderable truck is only the top trim.

He then said the extension is not the smartest move from a profit-maximizing standpoint and framed it as sentimentality. He gave no exact end date, backlog size, or extra-unit target, and he did not say every outstanding order will be built. Factory space is still being reserved for Cybercab. By November 13 the U.S. configurator still offered only Cyberbeast. The headline is an extension. The production program still ends in 2027, with refunds still expected and no replacement volume named for the truck.

keyChanges.title: $41,990 Model Y AWD pulled as Premium and Model Y L orders slip into 2027
keyChanges.description: Tesla removed the $41,990 Model Y AWD from the U.S. configurator after about nine months (it launched in February 2026 at 294 miles and a 4.6-second 0-60). A November 12 Seattle 98101 check found the $39,990 rear-wheel-drive model still listed and the cheapest new all-wheel-drive order now the $49,990 Premium AWD, an $8,000 step up. Tesla gave no explanation. Inventory AWD units can still appear. The same check put Premium RWD at $45,990 and Premium AWD at $49,990 on January-March 2027 estimates ($47,630 and $51,630 with destination and order fees). In a September 22 check the $41,990 AWD was still offered with December-January windows. Not a Tesla App's November 13 check said every Model Y Premium trim is sold out for 2026, with windows moved from December 2026-January 2027 to January-March 2027, and the six-seat Model Y L Launch Series moved from January-March 2027 to February-April 2027 at the same $61,990 ($63,630 with fees, 332 miles). New Premium and Model Y L orders therefore miss Q4. On November 14 the base Model Y RWD EPA rating on Tesla's site was 348 miles, up from 321, at the same $39,990 and the same 69 kWh pack, 6.8-second 0-60, and 125 mph top speed. Tesla has not said what changed. The range sticker is a spec change on the remaining cheap trim, while the AWD entry point and the 2026 delivery window for higher trims both got worse.

keyChanges.title: Grimes Terafab land tops 10,000 acres as SpaceX widens records fight
keyChanges.description: KBTX checked Grimes Central Appraisal District records and found WIT TECH LLC, the entity tied to Terafab, now holds more than 70 active accounts covering more than 10,000 acres around the project, up from the more than 7,700 acres the station counted in August. A bigger footprint is not a factory. The same report says those property records and the job listings do not establish construction status, and nothing in them shows a line that can make a chip. On Nov. 9 SpaceX amended its suit against the attorney general and Grimes County to challenge the August ruling on KBTX's own June request for tax-incentive files, economic analyses, and county correspondence. The attorney general had already said the county must release the non-privileged remainder. SpaceX is asking the court to keep negotiating documents, financial information, and employee-identifying information sealed for a private review. The citizens group that joined the case on Oct. 28 is still pushing for the tax-abatement records. KBTX counted 84 Terafab openings on Tesla's careers site, against SpaceX's earlier claim of 3,000 permanent jobs. Gov.-elect Hinojosa takes office in January already demanding more transparency on Musk-company incentives. More acres and a wider secrecy suit do not move the project any closer to making silicon.

keyChanges.title: Terafab's Japan tool push is supplier talks on an outlandish clock, not orders
keyChanges.description: Nikkei reported Nov. 10 that Terafab procurement managers visited Japan earlier in November and opened talks with chip-equipment suppliers, and that some were asked to deliver tools within a few months. Nikkei described the reaction inside the supply chain as excitement mixed with bewilderment at demands some see as outlandish. ChosunBiz and the Seoul Economic Daily, both retelling that Nikkei account, add the split described to suppliers: about 700,000 memory wafers and more than 300,000 logic wafers a month after 2032, about 40 times the 25,000-wafer monthly capacity at Rapidus's Hokkaido plant, plus a second-half-2028 mass-production target Musk had already floated. TeslaNorth's Nov. 10 write-up is the careful version: Tesla and SpaceX have not confirmed the schedule or the split, the million-wafer figure is a previously reported ambition rather than installed capacity, and a leading-edge fab typically takes more than three years from planning to production. Ground broke in Grimes County only in August 2026. Headlines that say Terafab placed orders or accelerated the plant overstate meetings. Supplier conversations do not fund the build, and they do not put a chip on a line that still is not producing.

keyChanges.title: House data-center bill leaves Terafab's existing JETI deal in place
keyChanges.description: Rep. Vincent Perez filed House Bill 732 on Nov. 9. The introduced text would deny new Chapter 312 abatements, Chapter 380 and 381 grants, tax-increment subsidies, Texas Enterprise Fund grants, and new JETI eligibility to a data center, defined as a facility whose primary use is processing, storing, or transmitting digital information, including training or running an AI model. The definition leaves out equipment that only supports a manufacturing operation when housing that equipment is not the site's primary use. Section 7.01 limits the ban to agreements signed, renewed, extended, or increased on or after the act's effective date of Sept. 1, 2027, and only if the bill actually passes. Terafab's existing JETI agreement is not voided by the filing. KBTX noted on Nov. 13 that the Grimes project already holds a JETI break, and separately that Terafab is a semiconductor plant rather than a data center. A building whose primary use is AI-model training would be ineligible for a new subsidy; a manufacturing fab is outside that definition. The politics are still hostile — the governor-elect has attacked the break, and a Democratic House is drafting incentive limits — but this text is a grandfathered draft, not a repeal.
